scenarios.title: A decayed creature is sacrificed at end of combat when it attacks
decisions: A declares Rot-Curse Rakshasa as an attacker against B.
B declares no blockers; combat damage is dealt.
At the end of combat step the decayed delayed trigger resolves.

variants.label: attacks
variants.expected: Rot-Curse Rakshasa deals 5 combat damage to B (life 15). At end of combat it is sacrificed and moves to A's graveyard.

variants.label: stays_home
variants.expected: Nothing is sacrificed. Rot-Curse Rakshasa stays on the battlefield and B's life stays 20.

detector.outcome: A decayed creature's attack trigger fires when that creature attacks, setting up its sacrifice at end of combat.
detector.near_miss: A decayed creature's attack trigger is evaluated against another creature's attack and does not fire.

scenarios.title: A decayed creature can't block
decisions: A declares Grizzly Bears as an attacker against B.
B tries to declare Rot-Curse Rakshasa as a blocker of Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: decayed_blocker
variants.expected: Rot-Curse Rakshasa is not a legal blocker, so the block is not legal and Grizzly Bears is unblocked. B takes 2 damage (life 18) and Rot-Curse Rakshasa stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: ordinary_blocker
variants.delta: B's creature is Hill Giant instead of Rot-Curse Rakshasa.
variants.expected: The block is legal. Hill Giant deals 3 damage to Grizzly Bears, which is destroyed, and takes 2 damage. B's life stays 20.

detector.outcome: A creature that a static ability forbids from blocking sits outside the legal blockers.
detector.near_miss: A creature that no static forbids sits among the legal blockers.
